strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of DNS Protocol Misuse for Command and Control

analytics.name: Analytic 2099
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an ICS Windows asset bypassing designated DNS resolvers, generating tunneling-like DNS content, or establishing HTTPS/TLS sessions to unapproved DoH resolver/API infrastructure from a process not authorized for encrypted DNS. Require a resolver-policy or asset-role violation plus suspicious query/content/process/destination evidence; suppress approved browsers, security products, vendor cloud services, and documented maintenance.

tuning.description: Site DNS resolvers and forwarding architecture
Explicitly permitted DoH/DoT endpoints, if any
Browsers/security/vendor software permitted to use encrypted DNS
Length/entropy/type/frequency patterns used only as corroboration
ICS assets that should not resolve/connect externally

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Sysmon
log_sources.channel: EventCode=3; connection to DNS/DoH destination with process identity

log_sources.name: NSM:DNS
log_sources.channel: Native DNS query/response content: long/encoded labels, TXT use, unusual query structure

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: Direct external DNS or HTTPS/TLS flow bypassing designated resolver/proxy

analytics.name: Analytic 2097
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies ICS clients sending DNS directly to unauthorized resolvers, native DNS with tunneling characteristics, or HTTPS/TLS connections to known/identified DoH infrastructure that bypass the site resolver/proxy architecture. Alert on policy violation plus content/flow corroboration; do not alert solely on high DNS volume.

tuning.description: Authorized recursive resolvers/forwarders
Permitted encrypted DNS services
Which ICS zones/assets may resolve externally
Encoded/long labels, unusual types, entropy and periodicity as corroboration
Resolver/API destinations used to identify bypass

log_sources.name: NetworkDevice:IDS
log_sources.channel: DoH/DoT identification, SNI/HTTP host when observable, DNS tunneling signatures

analytics.name: Analytic 2098
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a Linux ICS asset bypassing designated DNS resolvers, producing tunneling-like native DNS, or connecting to unapproved DoH/DoT infrastructure from an unauthorized process/service. Require resolver-policy or asset-role violation plus corroborating process, query, or destination evidence; suppress approved package/vendor/security workflows.

tuning.description: Site DNS resolvers
Permitted encrypted DNS endpoints
Services permitted to resolve externally
Tunneling-like query characteristics as corroboration
Assets with no legitimate external resolution

log_sources.name: linux:osquery
log_sources.channel: socket_events to DNS/DoH/DoT destinations, where deployed

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: External DNS/HTTPS/TLS flow bypassing approved resolver/proxy

analytics.name: Analytic 2096
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an embedded OT/IoT device sending DNS to a resolver not defined for its role, tunneling-like native DNS, or direct HTTPS/TLS to an unapproved DoH endpoint. Because many embedded devices have fixed communications, require deviation from the device-specific resolver/destination profile and corroborating query or destination evidence.

tuning.description: Expected DNS resolver(s) per device/model/site
Vendor/cloud domains required for operation
Permitted encrypted DNS, normally empty for fixed-function devices
Devices that should not resolve externally
Tunneling characteristics used as corroboration, not sole trigger

log_sources.name: NSM:TLS/HTTP
log_sources.channel: SNI/HTTP host or resolver endpoint identification when observable
